name: Whiteboard
use_label: Design software with your coding agent
one_liner: A desktop canvas where your coding agent draws diagrams of the software it is building, next to the code.

text.why: When an agent rewrites a lot of code, following how the pieces connect from text alone is hard. Whiteboard puts people and agents on one canvas to design the structure together: the agent draws the flow, and you can ask it in plain words to redraw it another way.
text.take: Instead of reading an agent's explanation as text, you get a diagram — and you keep the conversation going on the diagram itself.
build: A desktop app for macOS and Fedora. Connect a coding agent such as Claude Code or Codex from the welcome screen, and the agent uses an SDK to draw on the in-app canvas. The write-up, the flow diagram and the code it describes sit side by side.

who.role: Developers and teams who design and review larger changes together with a coding agent.

start.text: Download the app from install.dev.fast, open it, and connect Claude Code or Codex from the welcome screen.

caveat: Per the README, downloads exist only for macOS and Fedora. It is only useful alongside a coding agent you already run.

license.scope_text: Use, change and redistribute, commercially too. Keep the notice.

numbers.star_delta_unit: GitHub stars gained in the window, GH Archive events summed to as_of
numbers.method: Star total = the value last checked on GitHub (stars_checked_at) + increases observed via GH Archive since. The 24h · 7d · 30d gains are GH Archive hourly events summed to the reference time (as_of). No score of ours.

images.alt: Whiteboard: a design write-up with a flow diagram in the middle, the code on the right, and the agent conversation at lower left.

notes: This file was produced by the same build, from the same data, as the tesign.com item page. The text is editorial; the numbers are stored observations.
null in the JSON means not observed — never zero. The Markdown writes [unconfirmed] for it.
